segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. A **completeness map of JavaScript's standard built-in objects** (the MDN "standard built-in objects" surface + the ubiquitous Web globals) — companion to the [Node modules](NODE-MODULES.md) and [TypeScript features](TYPESCRIPT-FEATURES.md) indexes. It says, at a glance, which built-ins are supported, which work with real limits, which are not started, and which are out of scope for a **whole-program AOT compiler with fixed-shape objects and no runtime JS engine**. This page is **informational**: its rows are *not* counted toward the coverage percentages — the detailed, counted pages (linked per row) carry the per-method detail and the real numbers.

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format). ✅ = the built-in works (see its detail page for caveats); ❌ = not available today. Note: a ✅ here is a *loose* ✅ — per the project's rule, any caveat excludes a row from Strict Coverage, so several built-ins in the first table also appear with their residual limits in the second.

rows.feature: `Function` instances — `name`, `length`, util.inspect form (`[Function: f]`, `[AsyncFunction: f]`, `bound f`, `[class X]`, …), `toString()` source text, identity
notes: `Function.prototype` is a value: a function doing nothing whose `toString`/`call`/`apply`/`bind` act on their receiver; a function or class value reads them unbound, and `Object.getPrototypeOf` gives `Function.prototype` for a function or base class and the base class for a derived one ([ADR-01725](../adr/01/ADR-01725.md))

Names follow ECMAScript NamedEvaluation (binding, property key, assignment target, default, class field); `length` counts the parameters before the first default/rest one; the same holds through `any` and for built-in Error constructors ([ADR-01093](../adr/01/ADR-01093.md))

Own properties (`f.x = 1`, `Object.defineProperty(f, …)`, a TypeScript expando declaration), through `any` too, and in its inspect form (`[Function: f] { x: 1 }`) ([ADR-01232](../adr/01/ADR-01232.md))

`toString()` gives a function's or class's source text with its type syntax blanked, as Node's type stripping leaves it; a function unboxed from `any` keeps its identity ([ADR-01725](../adr/01/ADR-01725.md))
`toExponential()` with no argument uses the shortest round-trip mantissa (`(12345).toExponential()` → `1.2345e+4`), as in Node ([ADR-00832](../adr/00/ADR-00832.md))
`Math.max`/`Math.min` accept any arity: zero args give the JS identity (`-Infinity`/`+Infinity`), one arg returns that value, as in Node ([ADR-00831](../adr/00/ADR-00831.md))

The program's frames, named and positioned as V8 does: functions, `Object.m`, `Class.method`/`new Class`, `Type.fn [as prop]` for a call through a property, `Object.<anonymous>` for a CommonJS file's top level, and `at async fn` for the async functions awaiting the current one; also printed by `console.log(err)` and the uncaught report. See [ADR-01678](../adr/01/ADR-01678.md)
caveats: `captureStackTrace`'s `constructorOpt` is matched by the function's name, not its identity
V8's builtin frames (`at Array.map (<anonymous>)`) are not shown
The uncaught-exception report leaves out Node's source excerpt and `Node.js vX` line
`Error.prepareStackTrace` is not supported

notes: `.toString()` / `String(err)` / `` `${err}` `` render `name: message` as in Node. See [ADR-00846](../adr/00/ADR-00846.md)
`console.log(err)` shows the options' cause after the own properties as `[cause]: …`, as util.inspect does ([ADR-01418](../adr/01/ADR-01418.md))
caveats: The error-options second argument must be a `{ cause: <expr> }` object **literal** — a variable/computed options bag is a clean rejection ([ADR-01007](../adr/01/ADR-01007.md)); `AggregateError` takes no options (its `.cause` reads `undefined`)
`console.log(err)` leaves out the `[cause]: undefined` line of an error made with `{ cause: undefined }`

notes: A Symbol keeps its identity inside an `any` (hidden type-id word): `typeof` → `"symbol"` and narrows, `===`, `.description`, `Symbol(desc)` rendering, and ToNumber (`Number(x)`, a `TypedArray.set` offset, `+x`/`x * 1` under `-compat=js`) throws the spec's `TypeError` ([ADR-01059](../adr/01/ADR-01059.md))

caveats: `cleanupSome` (non-standard) rejected; aggregate held types (arrays, nullable scalars) rejected
Same-thread V1: a worker's registrations are flushed only by its own thread, not the process exit hook
Under `-mm=gc`, firing depends on the target actually being collected (conservative scanning can pin a stack-reachable pointer — same posture as the `WeakRef` tests)
notes: Mode-dependent timing, one API ([TDD-00163](../tdd/TDD-00163.md)/[ADR-00701](../adr/00/ADR-00701.md)): `-mm=manual` fires deterministically at `Memory.free(target)` plus an exit flush for survivors; `-mm=gc` fires via a real Boehm finalizer (observable after `gc()`); `-mm=auto`'s compiler-inserted frees are the same death signal — a registered target's cleanup fires deterministically at its scope exit ([ADR-00703](../adr/00/ADR-00703.md)), and the same exemption serves explicit `@free`/`@owned` in manual mode. Callbacks run on the microtask drain points, never synchronously at the death site
`-finalizers=report` prints one labeled leak line per registration never freed at exit (held value + `register()` call site) — the manual-memory leak detector
`register`/`unregister` with tokens; `-compat=js` dynamic-object targets unbox like WeakMap keys; `held === target` is a compile error when statically obvious

segments.text:
## Partial — works, with real caveats

Each compiles and runs for its core case but carries a limitation, mostly driven by the fixed-shape runtime, byte-sequence strings, or the absence of a locale/ICU layer. The linked detail page has the specifics.

caveats: `.normalize()` **missing** (no Unicode tables); `.matchAll()` eager not lazy; `.localeCompare()` ignores `locales` (root order) → [String methods](STRING-METHODS.md)
length-mutating methods propagate to caller only for plain **variable** params (not object-field/array-element receivers); `.flat(depth)` needs a constant depth → [Array methods](ARRAY-METHODS.md)

prototype machinery, descriptors, accessors exist on **`any`-typed / js-mode dynamic objects only**; static structs are fixed-shape (no dynamic add/delete, no prototype) → [Object, Map & Set](OBJECT-COLLECTIONS.md)
a bigint or a symbol has no wrapper object: `Object(1n)` / `Object(sym)` is a compile error for a typed value and returns the primitive itself for an `any`
missing `construct`; the object methods require a dynamic target → [Object, Map & Set](OBJECT-COLLECTIONS.md)
only `get`/`set`/`has`/`deleteProperty`/`ownKeys`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor` traps; dynamic target only → [Object, Map & Set](OBJECT-COLLECTIONS.md)
`toString(radix)` non-power-of-two fractional trailing-digit divergence; `toPrecision` fixed/exp threshold differs → [Number & Math](NUMBER-MATH.md)
`thisArg` binds only a `this: T` parameter (no method-borrowing of a class method); not on a Node module's functions → [Language constructs](LANGUAGE-CONSTRUCTS.md)

Of the well-known symbols the runtime honors `Symbol.iterator`, `Symbol.asyncIterator` and `Symbol.toPrimitive`, `Symbol.species` as a class's static getter (extending Array, a typed array or Promise), and `Symbol.toStringTag` as a class getter; an object literal's `toStringTag` member, `hasInstance` and the rest are values only → [Type system](TYPE-SYSTEM.md)
`u`/`d` flags **missing** (accepted, not implemented) → [RegExp](REGEXP.md)
a strict-lane literal mixing two object types is rejected → [JSON](JSON.md)
`resize`/`grow` need `{maxByteLength}`; views don't length-track resize → [Binary data & typed arrays](BINARY-DATA-TYPED-ARRAYS.md)
UTF-8 only; non-UTF-8 labels throw `RangeError` at construction → [Encoding & text](ENCODING-TEXT.md)
`AbortSignal` isn't wired into `setTimeout` → [Events & cancellation](EVENTS-CANCELLATION.md)
literal-only algorithm dispatch; ops throw synchronously rather than rejecting; `CryptoKey.algorithm`/`.usages` unimplemented → [Web Crypto](WEB-CRYPTO.md)
Setters need a named-variable receiver; no locale/`Intl` formatting; `toString`'s zone name covers the common zones only → [Performance timing](PERFORMANCE-TIMING.md)
`eventLoopUtilization`/`nodeTiming` missing → [Performance timing](PERFORMANCE-TIMING.md)
general/dynamic eval **missing**; only a compile-time-constant `eval("<expression>")` static subset works → [Global functions](GLOBAL-FUNCTIONS.md)

## Not started (in scope)

Standard built-ins that fit the model and would add value, not yet built.

caveats: `Iterator.from` and the global `Iterator` constructor (`instanceof Iterator`, `extends Iterator`) are missing
notes: `map`, `filter`, `take`, `drop`, `flatMap` (lazy, closing the source on `return()`), `reduce`, `toArray`, `forEach`, `some`, `every` and `find` on generators and the Array, Map and Set iterators, also through `any`, written in TypeScript ([ADR-01373](../adr/01/ADR-01373.md)); Node has no `AsyncIterator` helpers

caveats: a `newTarget` other than the target throws a TypeError rather than constructing with that prototype → [Object, Map & Set](OBJECT-COLLECTIONS.md)

notes: The opt-in embedded JS engine is not started (only the static-subset eval works) → [Global functions](GLOBAL-FUNCTIONS.md)

segments.text:
## Out of scope (by the whole-program AOT / no-runtime / fixed-shape model)

Built-ins that depend on a live JS engine, a locale/ICU layer, or a dynamic property/protocol model native ahead-of-time output has no equivalent for. Listed for completeness, not planned.

notes: No locale/ICU infrastructure — a bare `Intl` reference is an undefined-variable compile error; the reason `bigint.toLocaleString`/`Date.toLocale*` are gaps (`localeCompare` collates by generated ICU root-order tables instead, [ADR-01827](../adr/01/ADR-01827.md)). `Number.prototype.toLocaleString()` implements the **no-argument** en-US default (thousands grouping + max 3 fraction digits, [ADR-00847](../adr/00/ADR-00847.md)); a locale/options argument is a clean rejection
No runtime JS engine ([ADR-00022](../adr/00/ADR-00022.md)); only the static-subset eval works
Limited to the 6 dynamic-object traps; the rest have no interception point in the fixed-shape model
Objects are fixed-shape heap structs; dynamic add/delete + prototype links live only in the `any`/js-mode dynamic path by design

rows.feature: Well-known symbols as runtime protocol dispatch (`Symbol.hasInstance`/`toStringTag`/…)
notes: `Symbol.iterator`, `Symbol.asyncIterator` and `Symbol.toPrimitive` are honored — as own properties, class members and object-literal members — and `Symbol.species` as a class's static getter; the others are not consulted
